solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sunglasses but no sun initially? Hell!

indicators.note: but no tells us to take something away from the sunglasses word

parts.note: shades is an informal word for sunglasses

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word sun

explanation.surface: Someone finds sunglasses pointless on a sunless day and curses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no' removes S, the first letter of 'sun' picked out by 'initially', from SHADES.
explanation.definitionFit: The underworld of Greek myth is used as another name for hell.

clue.text: They offer special treatment — blister has dissipated

indicators.note: dissipated suggests the letters are scattered about

explanation.surface: A blister has cleared up after some alternative therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Practitioners of plant-based medicine offer their own particular kind of remedy.

clue.text: Like teacher, one about to be faced with 'Didn't do nothing!'

indicators.note: to be faced with means the following letters have the first piece in front of them

parts.note: if you did not do nothing, you did act
I is the Roman numeral for one
c is short for circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A teacher corrects a pupil's double negative.
explanation.walkthrough: The double negative in 'Didn't do nothing' read logically means DID ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to instruct, in the manner of a teacher.

clue.text: Stretch over to grab gold church vessel

indicators.note: to grab means the stretch word seizes and holds the next pieces

parts.note: to span is to stretch over, as a bridge does
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone reaches across to snatch a golden vessel from a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooking pot with a handle is a vessel in the sense of a container.

clue.text: One vehicle and another taking time at back of hospital

indicators.note: at back of says the following pieces come after the hospital letter
taking says the car picks up the next piece after it

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
taken as written
another vehicle, here a car

explanation.surface: A vehicle and a second one, towing something, wait behind a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One vehicle' looks like the start of the wordplay but is the definition; 'another' is a second vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cart pushed or pulled by hand is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: The man's son gives a cry of disapproval

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A father's boy jeers at something he dislikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp sibilant sound made by an audience is a way of showing disapproval.

clue.text: One saint entertained by some French believers of a certain type

indicators.note: entertained by means the French word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: des is French for some
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A holy person is hosted by a group of French believers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who believe in a creator god without revealed religion hold a particular kind of belief.

clue.text: A daughter evil — what can an agony aunt offer?

definitions.text: what can an agony aunt offer?

parts.note: vice is wickedness, evil

explanation.surface: A mother writes to a problem page about her wicked daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: An agony aunt is a British newspaper advice columnist who answers readers' personal problems.
explanation.definitionFit: An agony aunt's job is giving guidance to readers who write in with problems.

clue.text: Grasp a small branch

definitions.meaning: to understand something, informally to catch on
a slender shoot growing from a tree

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for realising or catching on, and also a thin shoot off a tree.

clue.text: Fortifications giving engineers suspicions

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
suspicions are doubts

explanation.surface: Engineers feel misgivings about some defensive works.
explanation.definitionFit: Small enclosed earthworks used for defence are a type of fortification.

clue.text: Fabulous activity for a vandal?

definitions.meaning: informal praise meaning wonderful or terrific
breaking things to pieces, what a vandal does

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for excellent, and literally means breaking things, a vandal's pastime.

clue.text: Mister Michael taken for saint? An ape!

indicators.note: taken for says one piece replaces the other in the word mister

parts.note: Mick is a familiar form of Michael

explanation.surface: A man named Michael is mistaken for a holy man and called an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken for' swaps ST in MISTER for MICK, giving MI-MICK-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy them, so an ape in this sense is an imitator.

clue.text: Senior worker terribly nice to have on board

indicators.note: to have on board means the worker holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of nice are knocked badly out of shape

explanation.surface: An old employee is awfully pleasant to keep on the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' makes CIEN for the ant to take on board; 'Senior' as a noun would be a person, but here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, and a senior is an older person, as in ancient retainer.

clue.text: Behind the barrier he hides

indicators.note: hides means the man goes out of sight, so his letters vanish from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
a railing is a fence-like barrier

explanation.surface: Someone hides behind a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' removes HE from THE RAILING, leaving T plus RAILING.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailing means lagging behind, as a team does when losing.

clue.text: Makes new recording of rock band with flowery group backing

indicators.note: backing means the flowers come along behind as support for the band

parts.note: REM was a well-known American rock band
asters are a group of flowers, daisy-like plants

explanation.surface: A rock band rerecords its songs with a backing group named after flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' is not a reversal here: the flowers act as the band's backing group, so they follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: To remaster is to produce a new master recording from an old one, so the phrase is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bad lad's bed's stuffed with silver in transportable containers

indicators.note: stuffed with means the rearranged letters are packed around the silver
bad suggests the letters are spoiled into a different order

parts.note: the word with its apostrophe gives its letters as written
the word with its apostrophe gives its letters as written
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A naughty boy's bed has been crammed with silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges LADSBEDS into SADDLEBS; 'stuffed with' puts AG inside to give SADDLE-BAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags hung over a horse or bicycle carry belongings, so they are portable containers.

clue.text: Send comic man Don out as deputy to the boss

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A comedian named Don is dispatched to stand in as the boss's deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the fifteen letters of SEND COMIC MAN DON.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the person ranking just below the commander, the boss's deputy.

clue.text: Ducks walk when crossing road

parts.note: a mall is a sheltered walk or promenade

indicators.note: crossing means the when word stretches across the road letters

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he left

explanation.surface: Ducks waddle as they cross a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mall is a famous ceremonial avenue in London, which is why a walk can be a mall.
explanation.definitionFit: Common wild ducks of this species are a familiar example of ducks.

clue.text: Examiner giving some passes so reluctantly

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An examiner grudgingly passes a few candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: One who evaluates work or candidates is an examiner.

clue.text: Reversing vehicle, one going into French river — transport going under!

indicators.note: reversing says the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: going into puts the numeral inside the river

parts.note: the Marne is a river in northern France
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A vehicle backs into a French river and ends up underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' makes SUB from the vehicle; the definition's 'going under' means travelling below the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that travels below the sea's surface is transport that goes under.

clue.text: Graduate introducing Holy Writ, not one for gibberish

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: not one means the numeral one, I, is dropped

parts.note: the Bible is Holy Writ

explanation.surface: A graduate preaching from scripture talks nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Babble is meaningless chatter, the same thing as gibberish.

clue.text: Join strike shortly before hour

indicators.note: before says the shortened word comes ahead of the hour letter
shortly means the strike word is cut short at the end

parts.note: to strike is to attack

explanation.surface: Unions plan to join a walkout just before the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach things is to fasten or join them together.

clue.text: About 50, one naughty female posing as 23!

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 23 down, a verb meaning to soothe

parts.note: re means about, concerning
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
Eve, who ate the forbidden fruit, is a naughty woman

explanation.surface: Around fifty, a mischievous woman pretends to be someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer at 23 down, EASE, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve pain is to alleviate or soothe it, the verb sense of the cross-referenced answer.

clue.text: Vandalism with a bottle circumvented by wise man

indicators.note: circumvented by means surrounded by, so the wise man goes around the bottle

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
a bota is a Spanish leather wine bottle

explanation.surface: A sage dodges a vandal wielding a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: A bota is an uncommon word: a Spanish leather bottle for wine; 'a' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate destruction or damage to property is vandalism, so wrecking work counts.

clue.text: Throw out container

definitions.meaning: to dismiss from a job or eject
a large bag for carrying goods

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to fire someone from a job and also a large bag.

clue.text: What an artist needs mostly is no bother

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: an easel holds an artist's canvas

explanation.surface: Asking what a painter needs is an easy question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of EASEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with no bother means doing it with facility.

clue.text: Great food from a mum — brother is about to tuck in

indicators.note: to tuck in means the brother pieces go inside the mother word

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: about turns the little word is round

explanation.surface: A mother's lovely cooking, which her brother is about to devour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes SI from 'is'; the leading A is the clue's own word 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth this was the food of the gods, so anything delicious is called this.

clue.text: Joint accommodation is what one offers desk worker

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
a hole is informal for a poky place to live

explanation.surface: Shared lodgings are what a firm provides for an office employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint accommodation' looks like a shared flat; it is a knee's space, with 'one' meaning a desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk provides a recess under it for the legs of whoever sits there working.

clue.text: Things hurting — therefore repose no end

parts.note: so means therefore

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the rest word is lost

parts.note: repose is rest

explanation.surface: Aching limbs, so a rest is needed without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Painful inflamed spots on the body are things that hurt.
